findings.text: The module-level _stub_exporter now supplies a passing gate verdict to 16 doubles from one edit. VERDICT: NIT - not the forbidden move, but the same shape one scope smaller. The brief forbade introducing a shared helper, autouse fixture, conftest patch or parametrised default that supplies all_gates_passed for more than one double at once, and the node did not: no conftest changed (tests/standard_names/conftest.py greps clean for all_gates_passed and gate_results), no new helper was added, and all seven edits are in-place modifications of pre-existing per-file factories and per-test closures. But _stub_exporter is shared by 16 of the 44 tests in this file - measured as the per-file failure count under my inversion probe - so a test added to test_review_release.py after today inherits all_gates_passed=True without stating it, which is the permissive default the wave is removing, reinstated at file scope rather than suite scope. TRIGGERING INPUT: a future test in this file that ought to exercise a gate refusal, written against _stub_exporter, silently gets a passing verdict and asserts a downstream outcome that a real failed export would never reach. Blast radius is one file and the fix is one line at the call site, so this is an observation for the next author, not a defect to hold the node on.

gate_results=[] is inert at all seven sites. VERDICT: NIT. catalog_release.py:2016-2018 reads gate_results only inside `if all_gates_passed is False`, so with the verdict True the empty list is never consulted at any of the seven construction sites. It costs nothing and it does arm the second half of the guard if a later edit flips a verdict to False - at which point the empty list would trigger the 'names no failed export gates' refusal rather than an AttributeError, which is arguably the better failure. The only cost is legibility: a reader of these fixtures may infer the gate-failure path is exercised here, when the tests that own it are test_release_gate_verdict_is_read.py:113/133 and test_export_report_gate.py:60.

Two release-flow export doubles still omit the verdict; both are currently unreachable by the guard. VERDICT: NIT, outside this node's declared write paths and reported rather than fixed. test_release_rehearsal_writes_nothing.py:98 returns SimpleNamespace(exported_count=len(review_batch)) with no verdict, and test_release_rehearsal_accounting.py:95 builds an _export_report helper with total_candidates, exported_count, exclusion_counts and exclusion_records and no verdict. VERIFIED they cannot reach the refusal: the rehearsal file's only run_review_release call (line 144) passes dry_run=True, and catalog_release.py:1964-1990 returns from the dry-run branch before the export leg at :1994; the accounting helper is consumed by _record_export_accounting / _rehearse_export_accounting, neither of which reads all_gates_passed. Both are therefore latent rather than live. TRIGGERING INPUT: change either test to a real cut (dry_run=False with the same stub) and it refuses immediately with the missing-verdict error - a red test, never a false pass, which is why this is a note and not a MUST-FIX.

justifications.durability: The chosen shape is the durable one - an explicit value at each construction site, which is what keeps a fail-closed production check readable rather than reinstating the default it just removed. Three residuals, none blocking. FIRST, test_review_release.py:63 _stub_exporter is a module-level factory shared by 16 of that file's 44 tests, so one edit now supplies a passing verdict to 16 doubles at once. This is NOT the forbidden move - the factory pre-existed the node and was not introduced by it, and its blast radius is one file rather than the suite - but it is the same permissive-default shape at file scope: a test added to that file later inherits a passing gate verdict without ever stating one, and nothing will report it. SECOND, gate_results=[] is inert at all seven sites: catalog_release.py:2017 reads gate_results only inside the `if all_gates_passed is False` branch, so with True it is never consulted. Harmless, but it reads as though the failure path were exercised here when the tests that own that path are test_release_gate_verdict_is_read.py and test_export_report_gate.py. THIRD, the invariant does not reach two sibling doubles - test_release_rehearsal_writes_nothing.py:98 and the _export_report helper at test_release_rehearsal_accounting.py:95 both omit the verdict. I confirmed neither can reach the guard today: the rehearsal file's only run_review_release call passes dry_run=True, which returns at catalog_release.py:1990 before the export leg, and the accounting helper is fed to _record_export_accounting / _rehearse_export_accounting, which never read the verdict. They are latent sites that would refuse loudly the day either test becomes a real cut, so the cost of leaving them is a future red test, not a false pass.
justifications.evidence: The strongest kind available for a fixture change, and it survives independent replication. The worker recorded a base reproduction at ce35cbf73 (23 failed, 39 passed focused), a repaired focused gate (62 passed, 1 deselected), and a full standard-names suite pair on all_debug whose failure/error id sets fall from 46 to 23, removing exactly the 23 assigned ids with zero added (removed_by_fixture_fix.txt 23 ids, unexpected_after.txt 0 ids). The negative control is the right one for this node - reverting only the verdict fields - and it names its mutation. I did not take that on trust: my own inversion, which never touched the repository tree and therefore could not have copied the worker's edit, returned 23 failures whose ids diff clean against the worker's list, refusing with "Export report is missing required verdict attribute 'all_gates_passed'; release refused because export success was not observed." The single reservation is aperture rather than rigour: no gate in this node pins that these doubles KEEP stating a verdict, which is acceptable only because the guard itself is that pin - remove the attribute again and 23 tests go red, which is precisely what my probe demonstrated.
justifications.fit: Idiomatic for this repository and for these files. It keeps the existing SimpleNamespace double idiom rather than importing a real ExportReport, places the new fields beside exported_count in the same constructor, and attaches a one-line comment at each site that names the mechanism and what the test actually owns ('Export gates are scaffolding; these tests exercise release orchestration' / 'report reachability' / 'review-body authorship' / 'checkout restoration' / 'preview-link handling' / 'baseline preservation' / 'sparse assembly'). No comment carries a plan label, stage name, ticket reference or author attribution, and no symbol or filename changed. Each of the three refusal-asserting tests among the repaired 23 keeps asserting its own refusal and nothing about gates - test_review_release_refuses_branch_with_unique_commits still asserts len(report.errors) == 1 plus the branch, old head and both recovery commands; test_report_missing_from_checkout_refuses_the_request still asserts ExportReportLinkError; test_release_names_missing_preview_link_invariant still asserts its exact ReviewPreviewLinkInvariantError string. That len(errors) == 1 assertion is itself the check that True is the right value: a False verdict here would add a gate error and fail the test. The comment prose is the only place to quibble - calling gate verdicts 'scaffolding' is true of these tests and slightly undersells that the attribute is now load-bearing.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node was to make every release-flow export double state its gate verdict after the paired guard stopped reading a missing attribute as a pass, and it does. Commit e2b8ee106 touches exactly seven export-report construction sites across the five assigned files - test_review_release.py:63 (the module factory), :474 and :651 (two inline closures), test_exclusion_report_is_reachable.py:109, test_review_body_authored.py:79, test_review_release_preview_link.py:63, test_review_release_checkout.py:56 - each adding all_gates_passed=True and gate_results=[] to a SimpleNamespace that previously carried only exported_count. The worker's own plan comment says 'seven construction sites', which is the accurate count; the brief's '23' is the repaired test count, not the double count. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY at the integrated head d31f8cb92: the five files run 62 passed, 1 deselected (head_focused.log), and an inversion probe that rebinds the SimpleNamespace name each module imported so every double it builds loses all_gates_passed produces 23 failed, 39 passed, with a failure id set BYTE-IDENTICAL to the worker's removed_by_fixture_fix.txt and the same 16/2/2/2/1 per-file distribution the plan comment claims (inverted_focused.log). 37 of the tracebacks carry the guard's exact refusal string. The one completeness gap: two release-flow doubles elsewhere still omit the verdict - test_release_rehearsal_writes_nothing.py:98 and test_release_rehearsal_accounting.py:95 - so 'every release-flow double' is not literally true, though neither can reach the guard today (see durability).
justifications.scope_discipline: Clean on every axis checked. git show --stat over both commits touches only the seven declared paths: five test files (42 insertions, 7 deletions - the 7 deletions are exactly the 7 replaced return statements) plus the two HTML documents. No production file changed: the diff contains no edit to imas_codex/, and no existing assertion line was modified anywhere - every '-' line in the test diff is a return statement. No conftest was touched and tests/standard_names/conftest.py contains no reference to all_gates_passed or gate_results, so the one move the brief forbade - a shared helper, autouse fixture, conftest patch or parametrised default supplying the attribute one layer out - was not made. The plan commit is additive only (5 insertions, 0 deletions), a single r-comment on section s2 with no plan-status, plan-version or meta change, and it explicitly states 'This worker does not resolve its driving followup or close the section'. The evidence archive gains 51 additive lines under an anchor the plan comment links by markdown, and that anchor resolves. Both commit subjects are conventional with bodies; neither carries an AI trailer, a plan label, a sprint id or a ticket number; nothing was pushed or merged by the worker.
